title: Disrupted metabolic support of intrinsic brain rhythms as a driver of spatiotemporal fragmentation in schizophrenia
title_zh: 精神分裂症中内在脑节律代谢支持受损导致时空碎片化的驱动因素
abstract: Schizophrenia can involve disturbances of lived time, lived space, and pre-reflective selfhood. This Perspective examines whether impaired adaptation of cerebral energy metabolism to changing neural demand could provide a physiological constraint on the temporal and spatial organization of neural activity relevant to these experiences. Evidence from cellular models, magnetic resonance spectroscopy, metabolic imaging, electrophysiology, and functional neuroimaging is synthesized, with emphasis on oxidative capacity, respiratory reserve, high-energy phosphate transfer, glycolytic regulation, and metabolic-neural relationships. Across these levels, bioenergetic abnormalities are documented in schizophrenia, but the available evidence does not establish a uniform metabolic deficit or a causal chain from cellular metabolism to psychopathology. A testable hypothesis is therefore proposed: impaired metabolic adaptation may limit neural reconfiguration across functional states, including oscillatory synchronization, intrinsic neural timescale flexibility, and large-scale network differentiation. A staged multimodal assay is outlined, combining functional [18 F] FDG positron emission tomography and electroencephalography during graded 40-Hz auditory stimulation. Primary analyses test metabolic and neural demand-response functions and their relative scaling; secondary analyses address within-condition coupling, recruitment and recovery kinetics, and dimension-matched associations with lived time, lived space, and self-experience. The framework extends spatiotemporal psychopathology by specifying a candidate physiological mechanism while preserving the distinction between neural and experiential levels. It generates falsifiable predictions for mechanistic, longitudinal, and therapeutic studies in schizophrenia.
abstract_zh: 精神分裂症可能涉及对生活时间、空间和前反思自我感的紊乱。本视角探讨了大脑能量代谢对变化的神经需求适应受损是否能为与这些体验相关的神经活动的时空组织提供生理限制。通过整合细胞模型、磁共振波谱、代谢成像、电生理和功能神经影像学的证据，重点关注氧化能力、呼吸储备、高能磷酸转移、糖酵解调节以及代谢-神经关系。在这些层面上，精神分裂症已记录到生物能异常，但现有证据并未确立统一的代谢缺陷或从细胞代谢到精神病理的因果链。因此提出了可检验的假设：代谢适应受损可能限制功能状态下的神经重构，包括振荡同步、内在神经时间尺度灵活性和大规模网络差异化。提出了分阶段多模态检测方案，结合功能[18 F] FDG正电子发射断层扫描和在分级40 Hz听觉刺激期间的脑电图。主要分析检验代谢与神经需求-响应功能及其相对尺度；次要分析处理条件内耦合、招募与恢复动力学，以及与生活时间、空间和自我体验匹配维度的关联。本框架通过指定候选生理机制扩展了时空精神病理学，同时保持神经与体验层面的区分。它为精神分裂症的机制性、纵向和治疗研究生成可证伪的预测。
